approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from previously accepted, scored molecules. It retains at most 64 survivors by score, draws parents from favored score bands, and either recombines connected fragments from two parents or makes a short sequence of ordinary single-parent mutations. A successful crossover receives an additional random finishing mutation with probability 35 percent before it reaches the candidate pool. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Valid, unique proposals fill a fresh surplus pool; a Gaussian process fitted to all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and correlated posterior draws to choose the announced evaluation batch. Accepted offspring update both the model archive and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove only the optional finishing mutation after a successful crossover, retaining its original random gate draw. The immediate recombinant must still pass the ordinary validity, identity and duplicate gates. Earlier siblings removed whole crossover or ordinary single-parent continuation; others changed recombination, parent scheduling or proposal lifetime. None isolates this finishing branch. Finishing can disrupt a completed structure, but the Parent also evaluates useful finished products and breeds from them, so the registered contribution prediction is a score decrease on removal. A complete contrary or negligible result would answer the same narrow question. This finishing-only treatment also supplies the separate control needed to interpret the parallel ring-recombination interaction.

observed_bottleneck: The specific behavior under test is a second random edit overwriting an already complete ordinary recombinant before learned pool allocation, with its separate endpoint value still unknown. In n-62daf219c70a the complete current-profile mean is 0.5956696497334577 with seed population SD 0.02659287062806747. A read-only audit of all 15 archived optimizer logs counts 75,961 distinct outer attempts, 34,334 crossover requests, 34,332 successful crossover opportunities and 12,307 finishing calls, all successful. Finished crossovers produce 12,029 pool entries and 531 real evaluations; 54 beat their best generating parent, 23 improve the incumbent, and 218 accepted identities later breed in 8,705 actual parent draws. Thirteen finished births occur in the terminal batch. These demonstrate use, not the causal scores of omitted edits. The audit is .slots/round-0023-slot-0/parent_finishing_plan_audit.json and counts repeated emitted receipts only as joins. Whole-crossover removal n-767d2ce08797 loses 0.054937284705486644, while ordinary-continuation removal n-dbee08307e86 loses 0.02686763734135833; those controls retain different boundaries and cannot identify finishing. The optional ring construction n-870ed6964d46 loses 0.04504628812412936; its typed new-cycle pattern persists in all 124 pure evaluated noncopy recombinants but only 43 of 55 finished ones. This selected structural association motivates an isolated finishing control without establishing that finishing is harmful. The limitation is unresolved productive exploration through this exposed branch, not a demonstrated benefit of preserving every immediate graph.
hypothesis: Remove optional post-crossover finishing mutation by setting its existing probability from 0.35 to 0.0 while retaining exactly one original gate draw after every successful ordinary crossover, so its immediate product reaches the unchanged admission pipeline without a finishing call; retain ordinary single-parent continuation and every other active Parent rule.

finding_summary.headline: Finishing contributes to endpoint search: its removal lowers the mean despite more local wins
finding_summary.insights:
The complete exposed removal supports a positive contribution from optional finishing in this exact exchange-disabled search composition. Earlier whole-crossover and ordinary-continuation controls did not answer this boundary. Preserving immediate recombinants clearly delivered useful evaluated and breeding products, yet that delivery was insufficient to preserve final search quality. More local wins were measured against weaker generating parents; they cannot substitute for the endpoint comparison. The result remains conditional: the gain in one seed and seven task/seed cells rules out a uniform benefit claim.

The molecules also do not support a simple chemical-preservation explanation. Mean size and ring count increased, but distinct typed core count decreased from 1,851 to 1,749. Tiny fragments and cumulenes became less frequent, while reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry persisted alongside useful conventional alternatives. Those are observed changes, not identified causes of the endpoint loss. Observed wall time increased from about 579 to 2,868 seconds, largely alongside higher oracle time on changed molecules, so fewer finishing calls do not establish a compute saving. The separate roles of missing finishing products, altered admission and random streams, and later adaptive feedback remain unresolved. This finding closes the exact finishing contribution question under the tested conditions; it does not establish whole-foundation value or the pending ring-by-finishing interaction.
finding_summary.results:
Finishing was absent at all 35,049 successful crossover opportunities, with 12,346 retained gate draws below the old threshold. Of those exposed immediate products, 9,907 entered candidate pools and 515 reached real evaluation. All 501 nonterminal accepted products entered the next model fit; 297 later bred. Fourteen births were terminal, and 204 other accepted products had later opportunities but were never reused.

All fifteen task/seed comparisons completed. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.559427, a paired change of -0.036243 against the registered 0.002 loss threshold. Seed changes were -0.059007, +0.020922 and -0.070644; eight task/seed endpoints declined and seven improved. Decoration hopping and docking had the largest mean losses, while zaleplon and median-2 means improved. Seed population dispersion fell from 0.026593 to 0.021675 around the lower mean. Across all accepted offspring, strict parent wins rose from 629 to 689 and incumbent gains from 258 to 264, but absolute offspring and parent scores were lower and the average positive incumbent step fell from 0.022510 to 0.019939.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic amides, cyclic amines and nitrogen-carbonyl polycycles retain reactive bonds and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Assessed Algorithm Node n-5a357a2ac96f against published Parent n-62daf219c70a. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory files were present and read in full: 9000 records altogether, including 4350 evaluated optimizer proposals on each side. Every task has 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals, across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The immutable brief reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with all supplied seeds matched and no profile-mismatched seeds. There are no missing paths or absent task/seed comparisons. The final_molecules digest excerpt contains late seed-2 proposals, not every seed incumbent; seed-specific bests and terminal proposals were read from the full files. The output consists of substituted indole/benzimidazole amides and strained arene-fused analogues, linked aza/oxygen polycycles, aryl cyclic amines, medium-ring nitrogen-carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Across tasks, supplied ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9724 to 0.9931 and aromatic-string incidence is 0.969 to 0.9839. These measure whether a molecule contains the text feature, not its ring count or fraction of aromatic atoms. Halogen-string incidence ranges from 0.2069 to 0.9713. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidence are 0.0 throughout; neutral strings nevertheless contain recognizable protonatable amines. A read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 audit of the trajectory SMILES parsed every evaluated optimizer proposal on both sides. Child heavy-atom counts have median 29 and mean 32.55, versus Parent median 28 and mean 28.71. Child mean perceived ring count is 4.49 versus 3.79, while the median is 4 on both sides. This is substantial cyclic and aromatic chemistry, with saturated nitrogen rings also present. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks but narrower among leading relatives within a seed; different strings and perceived ring counts do not establish independent useful scaffolds. The same audit finds N-halogen bonds in 1092 Child versus 1042 Parent optimizer records, O-halogen bonds in 545 versus 278, and O-O bonds in 272 versus 273. These are overlapping record-level incidences, not counts of distinct molecules or measurements of reactivity. Carbon-centred cumulated double bonds occur in 6 Child versus 52 Parent records, and proposals with at most 4 heavy atoms number 70 versus 119. Thus several liabilities persist while cumulenes and tiny-fragment exposure are less frequent. No emitted optimizer SMILES on either side contains an explicit tetrahedral or double-bond stereochemical marker; RDKit finds at least one unassigned potential tetrahedral centre in 2214 Child records. Perceived potential stereochemistry does not establish configurational stability. Ordinary aromatic halogens, amides, ethers, lactams and tertiary amines coexist with N-F/N-Cl, O-halogen, peroxide, strained-ring and unusual sulfur environments. Drug-likeness is weak overall and synthesis questionable, although individual conventional functional groups and some leaders are credible starting points for chemistry review. Valid SMILES and high oracle scores do not establish synthesis, stability, conformation or biological activity. The original gap reports for n-c55c3d520a2c and the baseline reproduction n-62daf219c70a were read through context.evidence_index; recurring gaps below preserve that provenance and are newly conditioned on this Child panel. Their recurrence or attenuation does not identify a responsible component, establish chemical mediation, or label any unobserved alternative molecule. Descriptor definitions, complete source-path hashes, per-seed examples and record-level derived chemistry are in .slots/round-0023-slot-0/molecular/chemistry_audit.json, trajectory_chemistry.jsonl and audit_chemistry.py. These are audit artifacts; this response is the only molecular_report. Parent molecules are described from their published trajectories, while every cited_smiles entry is verified against the Child digest or immutable-request trusted Child trajectory paths.

per_task.generated_character: The seed leaders are compact molecules with 24 or 25 heavy atoms and 3 perceived rings. Seed 0 retains an N-chloro indole anilide with dimethyl and vinyl-ether substitution. Seed 1 reaches an N-methyl anilide attached to a benzimidazole bearing vinyl, methyl and chloromethyl groups; it has an ordinary N-H ring nitrogen and no N-halogen bond. Seed 2 reaches an N-fluoro anilide on a benzene fused to an unsaturated four-membered ring, with hydroxymethyl, methyl and N-chlorinated hydrazino substitution. Thus the highest record is not simply another indole: its fused small ring and nitrogen attachments change the chemistry substantially. Mean proposal SMILES length is 43.2, and halogen-string incidence is 0.9103. Across all proposals, median heavy-atom count is 24, versus 25 for the Parent. The Parent leaders occupy related aromatic amide or vicinal-diketone territory; the Child shows alternative ring connectivity without resolving local reactivity concerns. Published Parent versus Child best observed scores, in seed order 0, 1, 2, are 0.394051 versus 0.425403; 0.474117 versus 0.449897; 0.438973 versus 0.451975. These compare complete seed histories, not matched molecular edits.
liabilities: Seed 0 has N-Cl on an indole nitrogen; seed 2 has an N-F amide and an N-Cl hydrazino attachment. These differ chemically from ordinary carbon-bound aromatic halogens.
The leading seed-2 arene-fused unsaturated four-membered ring raises geometry and stability questions. Aromatic labels on the neighboring benzene do not validate the fused ring.

The seed-1 counterexample to N-halogen dependence still carries a benzylic chloromethyl group, while nearby seed-2 indole relatives contain an O-N attachment. Removing one conspicuous liability does not make the whole family demonstrated synthetic targets.
missing_features: The record lacks a demonstrated stable alternative to the highest fused unsaturated small-ring/N-halogen arrangement at its exact score. The conventional benzimidazole ring and N-methyl amide at a nearby score are an important counterexample to an absolute inability to make ordinary nitrogen environments.
Chemically independent, plausible compact frameworks retaining the favorable aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are not consistently represented among the leading relatives within a seed.
A specific absent target motif cannot be inferred from these scores; there is no evidence that increasing ring count, halogen count or general polarity would supply it.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The three Child leading families reach 0.4254027310763201, 0.44989726212142783 and 0.4519753205796759. Benzanilide alone scores 0.000530067932312738, and ClCl scores 0.0; retaining an amide or halogen without the extended arrangement is insufficient. Conversely, a large joined indole-amidine/amide proposal at seed 2 evaluation 35 scores 4.122817481359723e-18, so more aromatic material is not generally rewarded. Chlorophenyl and fluorophenyl variants of the benzimidazole anilide both score 0.44989726212142783, and an N-fluoro indole amide reaches that same score. The visible association concerns a compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement and tolerated substitutions. It does not establish a required N-halogen bond, an exact missing pharmacophore, or a chemical advantage of the strained leading core.

per_task.generated_character: The three seeds reach distinct chemistry. Seed 0 produces a 29-heavy-atom, densely connected nitrogen/oxygen ring system joined by a thioamide, with an O-Br substituent. Seed 1 produces a 38-heavy-atom aminomethyl-linked aryl/pyridyl assembly carrying ethers, a fluorinated imine and vinyl-thioether chain; its leader has only 2 rings. Seed 2 produces the overall leader with 41 heavy atoms and 6 perceived aromatic rings: an aza/oxygen carbonyl bicyclic region linked through NH to a larger fused aza-lactone-like polycycle, with butyl, propoxy, methoxy and methyl substitution. That leader has neither halogen nor peroxide bonds. Across proposals, mean SMILES length is 82.8 and maximum length 233; mean heavy-atom count is 46.78 versus Parent 33.28. A seed-1 proposal reaches 120 heavy atoms, so the output includes very large assemblies despite smaller leaders. The Parent seed-0 best is a more compact, different nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione framework; its chemical organization is not reliably rediscovered in the corresponding Child seed. Synthetic plausibility varies from recognizable linked heterocycles to difficult ring junctions and reactive side chains. Published Parent versus Child best observed scores, in seed order 0, 1, 2, are 0.856148 versus 0.615965; 0.624821 versus 0.619801; 0.617802 versus 0.656390. These compare complete seed histories, not matched molecular edits.
liabilities: The seed-0 leader bears O-Br, and close relatives introduce O-S-Cl or N-Cl environments. A nearby carbon-chlorinated alternative retains a similar score and must be kept as contrary evidence to a necessary O-halogen role.

Seed-1 leaders combine an imidoyl-fluoride-like N=C(F) group, vinyl ethers or vinyl thioethers and long substituent chains. Their stored scores do not characterize local reactivity or physical properties.
O-O and O-O-O chains occur in high-scoring seed-2 relatives even though the best molecule has none; the final proposal retains an O-O-O ethyl substituent.
The very large tail and extensive aromatic surface introduce size and synthesis concerns. No solubility, stability or route evidence accompanies these structures.
missing_features: The output does not consistently supply compact, chemically credible alternatives to its favorable linked heterocyclic arrangements; substantial elaboration and reactive peripheral variations remain common.

The leading nonhalogenated, nonperoxidic seed-2 molecule demonstrates that such local bond environments are attainable. The remaining gap is reliable coverage of useful feasible frameworks across seeds, rather than absence of all stable heterocyclic chemistry.

Geometry and practical accessibility of the dense fused or bridged regions are unresolved. The supplied ordering does not identify an exact absent decoration or establish a general need for more rings.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in n-62daf219c70a; it recurs in n-5a357a2ac96f on the complete matched Search Seed panel at 300 observations per task. The present evaluated optimizer records include 1092 with N-halogen bonds, 545 with O-halogen bonds and 272 with O-O bonds, versus 1042, 278 and 273 in the published Parent. Counts overlap and measure bond occurrence, not physical reactivity. Leading relatives carry N-F, N-Cl, O-Br, peroxide chains, chloromethyl ethers or unusual sulfur bonding. Conversely, a leading linked aza/oxygen polycycle contains no halogen or peroxide, a benzimidazole anilide has no N-halogen, and an ordinary carbon-chlorinated relative scores close to its O-Br counterpart. The absent capability is reliable environment control, not an inability to make conventional heterocycles, amines or carbon-bound halogens.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments when retaining otherwise useful molecular frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need to distinguish heteroatom-halogen, peroxide and unusual sulfur environments from conventional substitutions, and offer chemically plausible alternatives while retaining relationships supported by accepted local feedback. Preserve the counterexamples: neither a universal halogen ban nor an automatic reward for replacing every flagged bond follows from these observations. This recurring chemistry gap has no identified component attribution or measured replacement benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This extends the ring-feasibility gap recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in n-62daf219c70a, with narrower current conditions. On the complete n-5a357a2ac96f matched Search panel, carbon-centred cumulene occurrence falls to 6 evaluated optimizer records from Parent 52; the leading Child families omit the Parent small-ring cumulene. Nevertheless, leaders contain an arene-fused unsaturated four-membered ring, related arene-fused three-membered rings, medium-ring nitrogen/carbonyl junctions, and aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen rings. Conventional pyrrolidine and fluorinated small carbocycles also appear, including at high scores. More rings and valid aromatic SMILES therefore do not by themselves resolve geometry, while the reduced cumulene count prevents treating the historical pattern as unchanged.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently resolve the geometric feasibility of fused small rings, medium-ring bridges and aromatic-labelled larger heterocycles.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need ring-size, unsaturation and junction-aware feasibility assessment together with alternative connectivities that retain useful functional-group arrangements. Distinguish ordinary small carbocycles from difficult fused unsaturation and bridges; do not infer a blanket prohibition of small rings or aromatic heterocycles. The observed changes in chemistry do not establish endpoint mediation or a score benefit from any proposed geometry constraint.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c, recurs in n-62daf219c70a, and remains in n-5a357a2ac96f under the complete matched Search conditions. Every supplied Child task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0, and none of the 4350 evaluated optimizer SMILES contains an explicit tetrahedral or double-bond stereochemical marker. RDKit identifies at least one unassigned potential tetrahedral centre in 2214 of those records, including substituted cyclic amines, fluorinated carbocycles, bridged frameworks and sulfoxide-containing molecules. Potential-centre perception does not establish configurational stability. Zero formal-charge-string incidence is a separate observation and coexists with clearly protonatable amines.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated molecular identities remain stereochemically unspecified even when their saturated or sulfur-containing environments admit potential stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation and its transformations need to preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemical identity where physically meaningful, while recognizing achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Assess protonation and tautomerism separately. These records show incomplete molecular definition; they do not demonstrate a stereochemical score penalty, a missing basic centre, or responsibility of any particular search component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in n-62daf219c70a; the n-5a357a2ac96f matched Search panel shows persistence with counterexamples. There are 70 evaluated optimizer proposals with at most 4 heavy atoms versus Parent 119, so small-fragment exposure has declined. Some isolated halogen or small reagent-like proposals still receive floor scores, while a late amino/sulfoxide/aryl fragment loses the cyclic context and scores 0.007925811229838719 against 0.7672225298102587 for that seed leader. At the other extreme, a 120-heavy-atom assembly scores 0.57781217750258, below a 41-heavy-atom linked-polycycle leader at 0.6563896336014299 in another seed of the same objective. A 21-heavy-atom cyclic amine approaches its observed score ceiling elsewhere. These are conditional structural associations across actual records, not a matched causal size experiment.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain useful functional-group context while avoiding both tiny fragments and excessive molecular elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local feedback should support context-preserving simplification and replacements while detecting when fragmentation removes the useful arrangement. The missing capability is consistent control of context and elaboration; neither a fixed minimum size nor a universal preference for smaller or larger molecules is justified. Keep chemically informative small high-scoring structures as counterexamples, and assess proposed alternatives through the allowed local feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This conditional coverage gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in n-62daf219c70a. It is re-observed in n-5a357a2ac96f at the supplied Search Seeds and observation budget: leaders repeatedly alter halogen location, short side chains, imino/carbonyl identity or ring segments within retained aromatic-amide, aryl-cyclic-amine and nitrogen-carbonyl families. Several peripheral variants have equal or very close scores. Different seeds reach distinct families, including a flexible aryl/pyridyl assembly and a fused aza/oxygen polycycle, so the full output is not globally collapsed and the generator plainly forms rings. The missing coverage concerns feasible alternatives among useful leading molecules, not raw SMILES variety.
transferable_gaps.gap: The leading outputs do not consistently include chemically independent plausible alternatives to a successful framework within each seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic structural transformations need to offer chemically independent connectivities that retain favorable functional and spatial relationships supported by current accepted feedback. Evaluate whether the resulting alternatives remain useful and chemically credible; new strings, more rings or greater core variety alone cannot establish improvement. Preserve the original source and these conditions when transferring the gap, rather than attributing convergence to a particular component or assuming that diversity necessarily raises the objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
